summary: The incoming P16 continuous-positive-complex-Hessian criterion, its arbitrary Hermitian-factor product formula and its non-Dini Hopf-surface product example are independently reconstructed in a 264-line inactive fragment with four proofs. The continuous-coefficient Fredholm extension includes its own contact-set minimum estimate, coefficient-free maximum-principle passage and compact-perturbation argument. Existing support-density bounds and the directional derivative theorem supply the final uniqueness implication. Original P16 remains open.
mathematical_checks: Continuous complex Hessian gives W2p through the Euclidean Laplacian, without full real C2 or Schauder regularity.
Radial local bounded-psh regularization and the finite background expansion identify the actual product with the continuous determinant.
Signed actual potential variations keep the scalar unchanged and force stationarity for each support.
The contact gradient area bound requires ellipticity but no coefficient derivative; smooth W2p approximation gives weak comparison, and a tangent barrier gives the strong maximum principle.
Uniform freezing estimates and compactness prove the continuous-operator Fredholm conclusion.
The exponent p=4n+1 makes support Lq density dual to W2p and fits the established subcritical bound.
All supports lie in one annihilator and probability normalization identifies them; the existing directional proposition supplies Gateaux differentiability.
Product stationarity is checked on every smooth function of all variables; it is identified with an actual support, rather than inferred solely from separated tests.
The Hopf surface metric is pluriclosed by the rank-one torsion identity; its stationary measure is its normalized square.
A positive continuous equatorial logarithmic modulus is non-Dini and non-Holder; the smooth factor cannot cancel its lower bound.
